newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia baulks at EU human rights-trade demand.
newsitem.headline: Australia baulks at EU human rights-trade demand.

text.p: Australia is refusing to sign a trade deal with the European Union, in part because it objects to demands to include a declaration on human rights.
"A human rights article of that kind does not belong to a trade and economic cooperation agreement," Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer told Parliament on Wednesday.
But the issue was not Australia's commitment to human rights, he said. "It's about the appropriateness of operative articles of this kind in the wrong type of agreement."
Inclusion of the articles would entitle the EU to unilaterally repudiate its trade obligations on the basis of some subjective objection to Australian policies, he said.
The EU routinely includes the human rights articles in trade agreements, and the Australian opposition said that if other countries were unworried by them then Australia should be too.
"The Republic of Korea recently signed such a framework agreement with the EU," said opposition trade spokesman Stephen Smith. "What do we have to fear on human rights that the Koreans don't?"
But Downer said Australia also objected to some of the trade issues in the proposed deal.
For example, Australian wanted greater market access for agricultural products, he said.
The proposed articles would say, among other things, that respect for human rights and democracy was the basis of co-operation between the parties.
